significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the conclusion that, across specified scientific laws, editing an internal mechanistic variable produces output changes with the law-predicted "direction and (approximate) magnitude," while matched correlates do not; this is a form-(iii) quantitative coupling supplemented by a causal distinction, not merely an existence claim. It would establish both a phenomenon—standard probes can systematically mistake correlates for mechanisms—and a mechanism-level result about which internal variables causally govern predictions, constraining model comparisons and the interpretation of observational findings such as the structure-associated attention analyzed by Vig et al. in “BERTology Meets Biology” (ICLR 2021). The per-mechanism positive and negative branches are distinguishable and informative: failures would undercut probe-based mechanistic interpretations, while calibrated successes would support them, although the aggregate prediction that "many" mechanisms fail is underdetermined because no threshold is given. Topic substitution fails: the generic topic would merit only a median score, whereas the specific law-calibrated intervention/correlate separation is the above-baseline contribution.

reach.justification: The named handle is the "Mechanism Fidelity Score aggregating direction agreement, monotonicity, and effect-size calibration," which could serve as an audit and model-selection diagnostic rather than merely an explanatory description. It can be used ex ante when selecting or trusting a model—the claim explicitly says it informs "trust, model selection, and hypothesis generation"—giving auditors an action window before downstream scientific use. However, the claim concedes that results are "model- and mechanism-specific," so re-extraction on another model supplies a procedure for looking but does not predict that model’s fidelity values; its asserted scope nevertheless spans protein, molecular, and physics/materials model classes and gives a handle to model auditors and selectors outside the immediate interpretability study. Topic substitution fails: the broad scientific-model topic alone would not supply this transferable audit score or its pre-use gating role, so the reach score rests on claim-specific content.
